cohort: 757 singleton pregnant women with confirmed placental abruption (PA) from a tertiary obstetrics hospital, categorized into preterm (n=300) and full-term (n=457) groups based on PA onset gestational age.
finding: Preterm placental abruption is associated with higher risks of severe maternal complications, including uterus-placenta apoplexy and ICU admission, and adverse neonatal outcomes such as fetal growth restriction and stillbirth, compared to full-term placental abruption.
mod_finding: Premature newborns had significantly less chances of forceps use compared to full-term newborns.
gest_age: PA onset after 20 weeks of gestation; participants were classified into preterm and full-term groups based on gestational age at PA onset.
